memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "(Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything the Lord commanded Moses; with him was Oholiab son of Ahisamak, of the tribe of Dan - an engraver and designer, and an embroiderer in blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen.)" - Exod 38:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In the middle of a materials inventory, Scripture pauses to name two men and their fathers and grandfathers.

God remembers the workers, not only the work.

Notice the phrase about Bezalel: he "made everything the Lord commanded Moses." Everything. Not most of it, not his own improved version of it. His extraordinary creativity operated entirely inside God's instructions — and it produced beauty, not blandness.

That is a helpful correction. We sometimes assume obedience limits creativity. Here, the most gifted artist in Israel worked wholly within God's design, and the result was magnificent.

Notice the two tribes as well: Judah and Dan. Judah was prominent, the tribe of kings and eventually of Christ. Dan was not. God partnered them without apology.

And notice Oholiab's listed skills — engraver, designer, embroiderer. Specific, practical, learned crafts. Scripture bothers to record them.

Your name is known to God, and so is your work. Whatever you have done faithfully — raised children, taught a class, run a business honestly, cared for a parent — is not lost. God is not unjust; He will not forget your work and the love you have shown Him (Heb 6:10).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe obedience restricts your creativity or channels it?
2. Whose work has God given you to partner with?
3. What faithful work of yours feels unnoticed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You know my name and see my work. Let everything I do be within what You have commanded. Amen.
